text:
jen p: Quick follow-ups from today's all-hands re: review cycle — dropping questions here so leadership / people ops can respond in one thread. TL;DR: timing, manager changes, and exceptions.

maria (People Ops): Thanks Jen — we'll answer inline. If anything needs a doc, I'll link it.

aj: Is the self-assessment window still 7 days after manager calibration or did that change? I thought there was a note about shifting windows.

maria (People Ops): Good catch. Window remains 7 days, but managers have an extra 48h grace for calibration edits only. Self-assessments must be submitted before the 7-day cutoff to be included in your packet.

jen p: If a manager leaves during the review window, what happens to pending calibrations / approvals? We've got a couple of teams with transitions.

maria (People Ops): When a manager exits during the review cycle we do a few things: 1) Temp manager assignment (auto) for approvals, 2) People Ops will flag affected packets and notify the director for manual sign-off, and 3) we keep the original manager's notes intact. Ping me the names and I'll escalate.

aj: Does that mean potential delays to payouts/merits? Any SLA?

maria (People Ops): We aim to keep payouts on the same cycle; regress only if we need additional sign-off. If there's a delay, we'll notify the impacted employees + people managers by EOD.

devon: For promotions: are IC->Senior (IC3->IC4) criteria updated? I heard new behavioral anchors were added.

maria (People Ops): Yes — small wording updates to impact and cross-team leadership. The rubric is in the packet doc (link below). Core deliverable expectations didn't change, it's mostly clarity on scope and stakeholder influence.

jen p: Can managers include cross-functional feedback after the self-assessment closes? Sometimes we get critical input late from product/ops.

maria (People Ops): Managers can append calibrated notes up until final sign-off, but any substantive late evidence submitted after self-assessments should be explained in the manager note. We don't reopen self-assessments, but context is allowed.

samir (CEO): Appreciate the questions. Short policy clarifications: 1) market adjustments are separate from merit/promotions and are handled by comp ops, 2) exceptional off-cycle increases still require director+HR approval, 3) if you feel a review was unfair, use the appeals form — People Ops will triage.

jen p: Where's the appeals form? I couldn't find it in the handbook.

maria (People Ops): Link: https://redwood.company/peopleops/reviews/appeal (bookmarking this tonight). Also adding a quick command: `/review-appeal` in Slack opens the form.

allhands-bot: Reminder: review docs updated 6m ago. Access: https://redwood.company/peopleops/reviews/rubrics (automated) :bell:

aj: Quick nit — are stock refresh timelines tied to review cycle now or still calendar quarter?

maria (People Ops): Stock refreshes remain quarterly; Q2 refresh will be processed after review outcomes, but approvals are independent. If you're expecting a refresh as part of a promotion, expect the grant to align with the next quarterly grant window.

devon: One last ask — can we get a short checklist for managers for the week after calibration? A 1-pager would help.

maria (People Ops): On it. I'll publish a 'Manager post-calibration checklist' PDF by tomorrow AM and drop here.

jen p: Awesome — thanks Maria + Samir. If anyone else has specific edge cases (sabbatical, parental leave, long-term contractors), please DM me and I'll forward to People Ops so we can include them in the checklist. :v:
